![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/140947c29667712d4a1071305396fff56a24f0a5c11f26e31368b8cc011f2863.png)

The area of one loop of the polar curve $r=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )$ is given by the integral

$$
A=\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}{cos}^{2}⁡(4\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Which of the following represents the total area bounded by the polar curve?
worked_solution:
The given polar curve is the polar rose with $2\cdot 4=8$ petals, and we know that the area of the first petal is

$$
A=\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}{cos}^{2}⁡(4\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Therefore, the total area bounded by the polar curve is 

$$
{A}_{\text{total}}=8\cdot A=12{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}{cos}^{2}⁡(4\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Question 4
?

The area of one loop of the polar curve r=3cos⁡(4θ) is given by the integral A=32∫−π/8π/8cos2⁡(4θ)dθ. Which of the following represents the total area bounded by the polar curve?

a
14∫−π/4π/4cos2⁡(4θ)dθ
b
16∫−π/8π/8cos2⁡(4θ)dθ
c
8∫−π/8π/8cos2⁡(4θ)dθ
d
12∫−π/8π/8cos2⁡(4θ)dθ
e
6∫−π/3π/3cos2⁡(4θ)dθ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given polar curve is the polar rose with 2⋅4=8 petals, and we know that the area of the first petal is A=32∫−π/8π/8cos2⁡(4θ)dθ.

Therefore, the total area bounded by the polar curve is Atotal=8⋅A=12∫−π/8π/8cos2⁡(4θ)dθ.
